scenes.narration: AI can only learn from what it's shown.
Welcome to FredsDesk, lesson eleven. In under a minute, you'll see why training data shapes everything an AI does.
Training data is the collection of examples a model learns from, such as text, images, or sounds.
scenes.definition: The examples a model learns from: text, images, sounds.

scenes.narration: Imagine learning a language only from song lyrics. You'd sound poetic, but ordering lunch would be rough. Everyday conversation gives you a wider range.
Three things matter most. Quantity: enough examples to find patterns. Quality: accurate, clean examples. And variety: many situations, not just one. Better data, better AI.
Imagine a model trained on dog photos, almost all taken on grass. Show it a cat on grass, and it may say dog. It learned the background, not the animal.

messages.text: Is this a dog? [photo: a cat on grass]

scenes.narration: Quick recap. One: training data is what a model learns from. Two: quantity, quality, and variety all matter. Three: narrow data makes a narrow AI.
points: Training data = examples to learn from

scenes.narration: Quiz time! If training data is narrow, the AI will be: A, great at everything, or B, weak outside what it saw? Answer in the comments. Tomorrow: why AI needs GPUs. Follow FredsDesk, and see you at the desk.
